title: Residency Drift Watchdog + Evidence Bundler for VPC/On-Prem
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a lightweight watchdog service that continuously evaluates customer configuration across data residency and retention settings against the canonical policy-as-code assertions and automatically packages cryptographically-signed evidence bundles for audits. This ticket covers the watchdog prototype, a minimal remediation orchestrator (safe-mode), and an evidence bundler compatible with the Console's audit export format.
acceptance_criteria: Watchdog samples configuration every 5 minutes for VPC and on-prem customers and reports any deviation from policy-as-code assertions to the compliance event stream.
Evidence bundler can collect: config snapshot, associated policy version, evaluation results, timestamp, and signed hash; and emits a tarball or signed JSON document that the Console can download.

Safe-mode remediation can flip a non-destructive, reversible setting (e.g., revert retention to a more restrictive value) only when an approval annotation is configured; otherwise it opens a high-priority incident with suggested rollback commands.
End-to-end flow covered by automated integration test that injects a simulated drift in a staging VPC tenant and validates detection, evidence bundle creation, and alerting to PagerDuty/Console.
Documentation (Confluence) describing the policy-to-watchdog mapping, evidence bundle schema, and operator runbooks is published and linked from the Console.
Performance: watchdog evaluation for a tenant with 150 resources completes in < 8s and memory usage stays under 250MB per Watchdog worker in the staging cluster.
technical_notes: Policy-as-code integration will reuse the existing policy-repo format used by ENG-22688 but must include a version fingerprint in the evaluation result.
Evaluation engine should be language-agnostic: use WASM sandbox for customer-provided assertions to avoid runtime dependencies and to simplify security reviews.

Evidence bundler schema: flat JSON with base64-encoded artifacts and a top-level signed SHA256 hash. Signature performed by the platform KMS; provide option to export unsigned bundle for air-gapped customers.
Use Kafka topic 'compliance.watchdog.events' for detection events. Events should include tenant_id, resource_id list, policy_version, severity, and evidence_bundle_url (if generated).
Minimal safe-mode remediator will call existing config-reconciler endpoint (ENG-31234) using a restricted service principal and will add audit annotations for any change.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): deploy watchdog as a single-replica job with feature flag 'watchdog:staging' and run synthetic drift scenarios (2/22 - 3/05).
Phase 2 (canary): enable for 5 low-risk customers on Dedicated for 2 weeks; collect performance telemetry and false-positive metrics (3/08 - 3/22).
Phase 3 (gradual): gate by account size and compliance tier; expose evidence download in Console and enable safe-mode behind explicit opt-in toggle (3/24 - 4/15).
Rollback: rollback via runtime-1.24 canary-kill switch if error rate > 2% or evidence bundles fail signature verification.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: false positives could cause unnecessary incidents. Mitigation: fuzzy-matching rules and a 10-minute debounce window before opening alerts.
Risk: evidence bundle could leak sensitive fields. Mitigation: redaction pipeline step configurable per-customer with allowlist of fields and mandatory review for PII rules.
Risk: KMS signing could add latency. Mitigation: async signing with local cache of short-lived signatures for staging and canary; full KMS signature for production bundles.
